0.2

NOTE: This ontology has been tweaked to allow it to properly generate the documentation for this site. For example, the ending of the ontology IRI was changed from a # to a / to allow hyperlinks to work correctly, this note was added, skos:definition annotations were derived from prov:definition (or editorsDefinition/rdfs:comment when definition is absent), and OWL restrictions are serialized inline with their class definitions.

docs.title: Activity
docs.text: An activity is something that occurs over a period of time and acts upon or with entities; it may include consuming, processing, transforming, modifying, relocating, using, or generating entities.

docs.title: Diagram
docs.text:

cluster_associated Activity Activity

docs.title: Specializations of Activity
docs.text: Class Description Accept Activity that identifies the acceptance of a resource (e.g., an article in a conference) Contribute Activity that identifies any contribution of an agent to a resource. Copyright Activity that identifies the Copyrighting activity associated to a resource. Create Activity that identifies the creation of a resource Modify Activity that identifies the modification of a resource. Publish Activity that identifies the publication of a resource Replace Activity that identifies the replacement of a resource. Rights Assignment Activity that identifies the rights assignment of a resource. Submit Activity that identifies the issuance (e.g., publication) of a resource.

docs.title: ActivityInfluence
docs.text: ActivitiyInfluence is the capacity of an activity to have an effect on the character, development, or behavior of another by means of generation, invalidation, communication, or other.

docs.title: Diagram

docs.title: Specializations of ActivityInfluence
docs.text: Class Description Communication Communication is the exchange of an entity by two activities, one activity using the entity generated by the other. Generation Generation is the completion of production of a new entity by an activity. This entity did not exist before generation and becomes available for usage after this generation. Invalidation Invalidation is the start of the destruction, cessation, or expiry of an existing entity by an activity. The entity is no longer available for use (or further invalidation) after invalidation. Any generation or usage of an entity precedes its invalidation.

docs.title: AgentInfluence
docs.text: AgentInfluence is the capacity of an agent to have an effect on the character, development, or behavior of another by means of attribution, association, delegation, or other.

docs.title: Diagram
docs.text:
SVG (interactive)PNG

cluster_associated Influence Influence AgentInfluence AgentInfluence AgentInfluence->Influence

docs.title: Specializations of AgentInfluence
docs.text:
Class Description Association An activity association is an assignment of responsibility to an agent for an activity, indicating that the agent had a role in the activity. It further allows for a plan to be specified, which is the plan intended by the agent to achieve some goals in the context of this activity. Attribution Attribution is the ascribing of an entity to an agent.

When an entity e is attributed to agent ag, entity e was generated by some unspecified activity that in turn was associated to agent ag. Thus, this relation is useful when the activity is not known, or irrelevant. | | Delegation | Delegation is the assignment of authority and responsibility to an agent (by itself or by another agent) to carry out a specific activity as a delegate or representative, while the agent it acts on behalf of retains some responsibility for the outcome of the delegated work.

For example, a student acted on behalf of his supervisor, who acted on behalf of the department chair, who acted on behalf of the university; all those agents are responsible in some way for the activity that took place but we do not say explicitly who bears responsibility and to what degree. |

docs.title: Formalization for AgentInfluence
docs.text: Property Constraint subClassOf Influence

docs.title: Delegation
docs.text:
Delegation is the assignment of authority and responsibility to an agent (by itself or by another agent) to carry out a specific activity as a delegate or representative, while the agent it acts on behalf of retains some responsibility for the outcome of the delegated work.

For example, a student acted on behalf of his supervisor, who acted on behalf of the department chair, who acted on behalf of the university; all those agents are responsible in some way for the activity that took place but we do not say explicitly who bears responsibility and to what degree.

docs.title: Derivation
docs.text: A derivation is a transformation of an entity into another, an update of an entity resulting in a new one, or the construction of a new entity based on a pre-existing entity.

docs.title: Diagram
docs.text:
SVG (interactive)PNG

cluster_associated EntityInfluence EntityInfluence Derivation Derivation Derivation->EntityInfluence

docs.title: Specializations of Derivation
docs.text:
Class Description Insertion Insertion is a derivation that describes the transformation of a dictionary into another, by insertion of one or more key-entity pairs. Primary Source A primary source for a topic refers to something produced by some agent with direct experience and knowledge about the topic, at the time of the topic's study, without benefit from hindsight.

Because of the directness of primary sources, they 'speak for themselves' in ways that cannot be captured through the filter of secondary sources. As such, it is important for secondary sources to reference those primary sources from which they were derived, so that their reliability can be investigated.

A primary source relation is a particular case of derivation of secondary materials from their primary sources. It is recognized that the determination of primary sources can be up to interpretation, and should be done according to conventions accepted within the application's domain. | | Quotation | A quotation is the repeat of (some or all of) an entity, such as text or image, by someone who may or may not be its original author. Quotation is a particular case of derivation. | | Removal | Removal is a derivation that describes the transformation of a dictionary into another, by removing one or more keys. | | Revision | A revision is a derivation for which the resulting entity is a revised version of some original. The implication here is that the resulting entity contains substantial content from the original. Revision is a particular case of derivation. |

docs.title: End
docs.text: End is when an activity is deemed to have been ended by an entity, known as trigger. The activity no longer exists after its end. Any usage, generation, or invalidation involving an activity precedes the activity's end. An end may refer to a trigger entity that terminated the activity, or to an activity, known as ender that generated the trigger.

docs.title: Influence
docs.text: Influence is the capacity of an entity, activity, or agent to have an effect on the character, development, or behavior of another by means of usage, start, end, generation, invalidation, communication, derivation, attribution, association, or delegation.

docs.title: Specializations of Influence
docs.text:
Class Description Activity Influence ActivitiyInfluence is the capacity of an activity to have an effect on the character, development, or behavior of another by means of generation, invalidation, communication, or other. Agent Influence AgentInfluence is the capacity of an agent to have an effect on the character, development, or behavior of another by means of attribution, association, delegation, or other. Association An activity association is an assignment of responsibility to an agent for an activity, indicating that the agent had a role in the activity. It further allows for a plan to be specified, which is the plan intended by the agent to achieve some goals in the context of this activity. Attribution Attribution is the ascribing of an entity to an agent.

When an entity e is attributed to agent ag, entity e was generated by some unspecified activity that in turn was associated to agent ag. Thus, this relation is useful when the activity is not known, or irrelevant. | | Communication | Communication is the exchange of an entity by two activities, one activity using the entity generated by the other. | | Delegation | Delegation is the assignment of authority and responsibility to an agent (by itself or by another agent) to carry out a specific activity as a delegate or representative, while the agent it acts on behalf of retains some responsibility for the outcome of the delegated work.

For example, a student acted on behalf of his supervisor, who acted on behalf of the department chair, who acted on behalf of the university; all those agents are responsible in some way for the activity that took place but we do not say explicitly who bears responsibility and to what degree. | | Derivation | A derivation is a transformation of an entity into another, an update of an entity resulting in a new one, or the construction of a new entity based on a pre-existing entity. | | End | End is when an activity is deemed to have been ended by an entity, known as trigger. The activity no longer exists after its end. Any usage, generation, or invalidation involving an activity precedes the activity's end. An end may refer to a trigger entity that terminated the activity, or to an activity, known as ender that generated the trigger. | | Entity Influence | EntityInfluence is the capacity of an entity to have an effect on the character, development, or behavior of another by means of usage, start, end, derivation, or other. | | Generation | Generation is the completion of production of a new entity by an activity. This entity did not exist before generation and becomes available for usage after this generation. | | Insertion | Insertion is a derivation that describes the transformation of a dictionary into another, by insertion of one or more key-entity pairs. | | Invalidation | Invalidation is the start of the destruction, cessation, or expiry of an existing entity by an activity. The entity is no longer available for use (or further invalidation) after invalidation. Any generation or usage of an entity precedes its invalidation. | | Primary Source | A primary source for a topic refers to something produced by some agent with direct experience and knowledge about the topic, at the time of the topic's study, without benefit from hindsight.

Because of the directness of primary sources, they 'speak for themselves' in ways that cannot be captured through the filter of secondary sources. As such, it is important for secondary sources to reference those primary sources from which they were derived, so that their reliability can be investigated.

A primary source relation is a particular case of derivation of secondary materials from their primary sources. It is recognized that the determination of primary sources can be up to interpretation, and should be done according to conventions accepted within the application's domain. | | Quotation | A quotation is the repeat of (some or all of) an entity, such as text or image, by someone who may or may not be its original author. Quotation is a particular case of derivation. | | Removal | Removal is a derivation that describes the transformation of a dictionary into another, by removing one or more keys. | | Revision | A revision is a derivation for which the resulting entity is a revised version of some original. The implication here is that the resulting entity contains substantial content from the original. Revision is a particular case of derivation. | | Start | Start is when an activity is deemed to have been started by an entity, known as trigger. The activity did not exist before its start. Any usage, generation, or invalidation involving an activity follows the activity's start. A start may refer to a trigger entity that set off the activity, or to an activity, known as starter, that generated the trigger. | | Usage | Usage is the beginning of utilizing an entity by an activity. Before usage, the activity had not begun to utilize this entity and could not have been affected by the entity. |

docs.title: InstantaneousEvent
docs.text: The PROV data model is implicitly based on a notion of instantaneous events (or just events), that mark transitions in the world. Events include generation, usage, or invalidation of entities, as well as starting or ending of activities. This notion of event is not first-class in the data model, but it is useful for explaining its other concepts and its semantics.

docs.title: Specializations of InstantaneousEvent
docs.text: Class Description End End is when an activity is deemed to have been ended by an entity, known as trigger. The activity no longer exists after its end. Any usage, generation, or invalidation involving an activity precedes the activity's end. An end may refer to a trigger entity that terminated the activity, or to an activity, known as ender that generated the trigger. Generation Generation is the completion of production of a new entity by an activity. This entity did not exist before generation and becomes available for usage after this generation. Invalidation Invalidation is the start of the destruction, cessation, or expiry of an existing entity by an activity. The entity is no longer available for use (or further invalidation) after invalidation. Any generation or usage of an entity precedes its invalidation. Start Start is when an activity is deemed to have been started by an entity, known as trigger. The activity did not exist before its start. Any usage, generation, or invalidation involving an activity follows the activity's start. A start may refer to a trigger entity that set off the activity, or to an activity, known as starter, that generated the trigger. Usage Usage is the beginning of utilizing an entity by an activity. Before usage, the activity had not begun to utilize this entity and could not have been affected by the entity.

docs.title: PrimarySource
docs.text:
A primary source for a topic refers to something produced by some agent with direct experience and knowledge about the topic, at the time of the topic's study, without benefit from hindsight.

Because of the directness of primary sources, they 'speak for themselves' in ways that cannot be captured through the filter of secondary sources. As such, it is important for secondary sources to reference those primary sources from which they were derived, so that their reliability can be investigated.

A primary source relation is a particular case of derivation of secondary materials from their primary sources. It is recognized that the determination of primary sources can be up to interpretation, and should be done according to conventions accepted within the application's domain.

Range: Dictionary

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/dictionary

docs.title: endedAtTime
docs.text:
The time at which an activity ended. See also prov:startedAtTime.

Domain: Activity

Range: xsd:dateTime

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/endedAtTime

docs.title: entity
docs.text:
The prov:entity property references an prov:Entity which influenced a resource. This property applies to an prov:EntityInfluence, which is given by a subproperty of prov:qualifiedInfluence from the influenced prov:Entity, prov:Activity or prov:Agent.

Domain: EntityInfluence

Range: Entity

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/entity

docs.title: generated
docs.text:
Domain: Activity

Range: Entity

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/generated

docs.title: generatedAtTime
docs.text:
The time at which an entity was completely created and is available for use.

Domain: Entity

Range: xsd:dateTime

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/generatedAtTime

docs.title: hadActivity
docs.text:
This property has multiple RDFS domains to suit multiple OWL Profiles. See PROV-O OWL Profile.

Domain: Delegation or Derivation or End or Start, Influence

Range: Activity

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/hadActivity

docs.title: hadDictionaryMember
docs.text:
Describes the key-entity pair that was member of a prov:Dictionary. A dictionary can have multiple members.

Domain: Dictionary

Range: KeyEntityPair

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/hadDictionaryMember

docs.title: hadGeneration
docs.text:
The optional Generation involved in an Entity's Derivation.

Domain: Derivation

Range: Generation

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/hadGeneration

docs.title: hadMember
docs.text:
Domain: Collection

Range: Entity

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/hadMember

docs.title: hadPlan
docs.text:
The optional Plan adopted by an Agent in Association with some Activity. Plan specifications are out of the scope of this specification.

Domain: Association

Range: Plan

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/hadPlan

docs.title: hadPrimarySource
docs.text:
Domain: Entity

Range: Entity

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/hadPrimarySource

docs.title: hadRole
docs.text:
prov:hadRole references the Role (i.e. the function of an entity with respect to an activity), in the context of an instantaneous usage, generation, association, start, and end.

Domain: Association or InstantaneousEvent, Influence

Range: Role

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/hadRole

docs.title: hadUsage
docs.text:
The optional Usage involved in an Entity's Derivation.

Domain: Derivation

Range: Usage

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/hadUsage

docs.title: has_anchor
docs.text:
Indicates anchor URI for a potentially dynamic resource instance.

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/has_anchor

docs.title: has_provenance
docs.text:
Indicates a provenance-URI for a resource; the resource identified by this property presents a provenance record about its subject or anchor resource.

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/has_provenance

docs.title: has_query_service
docs.text:
Indicates a provenance query service that can access provenance related to its subject or anchor resource.

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/has_query_service

docs.title: influenced
docs.text: IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/influenced

docs.title: influencer
docs.text:
This property is used as part of the qualified influence pattern. Subclasses of prov:Influence use these subproperties to reference the resource (Entity, Agent, or Activity) whose influence is being qualified.

Domain: Influence

Range: owl:Thing

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/influencer

docs.title: insertedKeyEntityPair
docs.text:
An object property to refer to the prov:KeyEntityPair inserted into a prov:Dictionary.

Domain: Insertion

Range: KeyEntityPair

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/insertedKeyEntityPair

docs.title: invalidated
docs.text:
Domain: Activity

Range: Entity

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/invalidated

docs.title: invalidatedAtTime
docs.text:
The time at which an entity was invalidated (i.e., no longer usable).

Domain: Entity

Range: xsd:dateTime

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/invalidatedAtTime

docs.title: mentionOf
docs.text:
prov:mentionOf is used to specialize an entity as described in another bundle. It is to be used in conjuction with prov:asInBundle.

prov:asInBundle is used to cite the Bundle in which the generalization was mentioned.

Domain: Entity

Range: Entity

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/mentionOf

docs.title: pairEntity
docs.text:
The entity of a prov:KeyEntityPair, which is an element of a prov:Dictionary.

Domain: KeyEntityPair

Range: Entity

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/pairEntity

docs.title: pairKey
docs.text:
The key of a prov:KeyEntityPair, which is an element of a prov:Dictionary.

Domain: KeyEntityPair

Range: rdfs:Literal

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/pairKey

docs.title: pingback
docs.text:
Relates a resource to a provenance pingback service that may receive additional provenance links about the resource.

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/pingback

docs.title: provenanceUriTemplate
docs.text:
Relates a provenance service to a URI template string for constructing provenance-URIs.

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/provenanceUriTemplate

docs.title: qualifiedAssociation
docs.text:
If this Activity prov:wasAssociatedWith Agent :ag, then it can qualify the Association using prov:qualifiedAssociation [ a prov:Association; prov:agent :ag; :foo :bar ].

Domain: Activity

Range: Association

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/qualifiedAssociation

docs.title: qualifiedAttribution
docs.text:
If this Entity prov:wasAttributedTo Agent :ag, then it can qualify how it was influenced using prov:qualifiedAttribution [ a prov:Attribution; prov:agent :ag; :foo :bar ].

Domain: Entity

Range: Attribution

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/qualifiedAttribution

docs.title: qualifiedCommunication
docs.text:
If this Activity prov:wasInformedBy Activity :a, then it can qualify how it was influenced using prov:qualifiedCommunication [ a prov:Communication; prov:activity :a; :foo :bar ].

Domain: Activity

Range: Communication

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/qualifiedCommunication

docs.title: qualifiedDelegation
docs.text:
If this Agent prov:actedOnBehalfOf Agent :ag, then it can qualify how with prov:qualifiedResponsibility [ a prov:Responsibility; prov:agent :ag; :foo :bar ].

Domain: Agent

Range: Delegation

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/qualifiedDelegation

docs.title: qualifiedDerivation
docs.text:
If this Entity prov:wasDerivedFrom Entity :e, then it can qualify how it was derived using prov:qualifiedDerivation [ a prov:Derivation; prov:entity :e; :foo :bar ].

Domain: Entity

Range: Derivation

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/qualifiedDerivation

docs.title: qualifiedEnd
docs.text:
If this Activity prov:wasEndedBy Entity :e1, then it can qualify how it was ended using prov:qualifiedEnd [ a prov:End; prov:entity :e1; :foo :bar ].

Domain: Activity

Range: End

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/qualifiedEnd

docs.title: qualifiedGeneration
docs.text:
If this Activity prov:generated Entity :e, then it can qualify how it performed the Generation using prov:qualifiedGeneration [ a prov:Generation; prov:entity :e; :foo :bar ].

Domain: Entity

Range: Generation

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/qualifiedGeneration

docs.title: qualifiedInfluence
docs.text:
Because prov:qualifiedInfluence is a broad relation, the more specific relations (qualifiedCommunication, qualifiedDelegation, qualifiedEnd, etc.) should be used when applicable.

Domain: Activity or Agent or Entity

Range: Influence

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/qualifiedInfluence

docs.title: qualifiedInsertion
docs.text:
prov:qualifiedInsertion shows the details of an insertion, in particular the inserted key-entity pairs.

Domain: Dictionary

Range: Insertion

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/qualifiedInsertion

docs.title: qualifiedInvalidation
docs.text:
If this Entity prov:wasInvalidatedBy Activity :a, then it can qualify how it was invalidated using prov:qualifiedInvalidation [ a prov:Invalidation; prov:activity :a; :foo :bar ].

Domain: Entity

Range: Invalidation

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/qualifiedInvalidation

docs.title: qualifiedPrimarySource
docs.text:
If this Entity prov:hadPrimarySource Entity :e, then it can qualify how using prov:qualifiedPrimarySource [ a prov:PrimarySource; prov:entity :e; :foo :bar ].

Domain: Entity

Range: PrimarySource

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/qualifiedPrimarySource

docs.title: qualifiedQuotation
docs.text:
If this Entity prov:wasQuotedFrom Entity :e, then it can qualify how using prov:qualifiedQuotation [ a prov:Quotation; prov:entity :e; :foo :bar ].

Domain: Entity

Range: Quotation

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/qualifiedQuotation

docs.title: qualifiedRemoval
docs.text:
prov:qualifiedRemoval shows the details of a removal, in particular the removed keys.

Domain: Dictionary

Range: Removal

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/qualifiedRemoval

docs.title: qualifiedRevision
docs.text:
If this Entity prov:wasRevisionOf Entity :e, then it can qualify how it was revised using prov:qualifiedRevision [ a prov:Revision; prov:entity :e; :foo :bar ].

Domain: Entity

Range: Revision

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/qualifiedRevision

docs.title: qualifiedStart
docs.text:
If this Activity prov:wasStartedBy Entity :e1, then it can qualify how it was started using prov:qualifiedStart [ a prov:Start; prov:entity :e1; :foo :bar ].

Domain: Activity

Range: Start

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/qualifiedStart

docs.title: qualifiedUsage
docs.text:
If this Activity prov:used Entity :e, then it can qualify how it used it using prov:qualifiedUsage [ a prov:Usage; prov:entity :e; :foo :bar ].

Domain: Activity

Range: Usage

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/qualifiedUsage

docs.title: removedKey
docs.text:
The key removed in a Removal.

Domain: Removal

Range: rdfs:Literal

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/removedKey

docs.title: specializationOf
docs.text:
An entity that is a specialization of another shares all aspects of the latter, and additionally presents more specific aspects of the same thing as the latter. In particular, the lifetime of the entity being specialized contains that of any specialization. Examples of aspects include a time period, an abstraction, and a context associated with the entity.

Domain: Entity

Range: Entity

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/specializationOf

docs.title: startedAtTime
docs.text:
The time at which an activity started. See also prov:endedAtTime.

Domain: Activity

Range: xsd:dateTime

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/startedAtTime

docs.title: used
docs.text:
A prov:Entity that was used by this prov:Activity. For example, :baking prov:used :spoon, :egg, :oven .

Domain: Activity

Range: Entity

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/used

docs.title: value
docs.text:
Provides a value that is a direct representation of an entity.

Domain: Entity

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/value

docs.title: wasAssociatedWith
docs.text:
An prov:Agent that had some (unspecified) responsibility for the occurrence of this prov:Activity.

Domain: Activity

Range: Agent

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/wasAssociatedWith

docs.title: wasAttributedTo
docs.text:
Attribution is the ascribing of an entity to an agent.

Domain: Entity

Range: Agent

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/wasAttributedTo

docs.title: wasDerivedFrom
docs.text:
A derivation is a transformation of an entity into another, an update of an entity resulting in a new one, or the construction of a new entity based on a pre-existing entity.

Domain: Entity

Range: Entity

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/wasDerivedFrom

docs.title: wasEndedBy
docs.text:
End is when an activity is deemed to have ended. An end may refer to an entity, known as trigger, that terminated the activity.

Domain: Activity

Range: Entity

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/wasEndedBy

docs.title: wasGeneratedBy
docs.text:
Domain: Entity

Range: Activity

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/wasGeneratedBy

docs.title: wasInfluencedBy
docs.text:
Because prov:wasInfluencedBy is a broad relation, its more specific subproperties (e.g. prov:wasInformedBy, prov:actedOnBehalfOf, prov:wasEndedBy, etc.) should be used when applicable.

Domain: Activity or Agent or Entity

Range: Activity or Agent or Entity

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/wasInfluencedBy

docs.title: wasInformedBy
docs.text:
An activity a2 is dependent on or informed by another activity a1, by way of some unspecified entity that is generated by a1 and used by a2.

Domain: Activity

Range: Activity

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/wasInformedBy

docs.title: wasInvalidatedBy
docs.text:
Domain: Entity

Range: Activity

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/wasInvalidatedBy

docs.title: wasQuotedFrom
docs.text:
An entity is derived from an original entity by copying, or 'quoting', some or all of it.

Domain: Entity

Range: Entity

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/wasQuotedFrom

docs.title: wasRevisionOf
docs.text:
A revision is a derivation that revises an entity into a revised version.

Domain: Entity

Range: Entity

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/wasRevisionOf

docs.title: wasStartedBy
docs.text:
Start is when an activity is deemed to have started. A start may refer to an entity, known as trigger, that initiated the activity.

Domain: Activity

Range: Entity

IRI: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov/wasStartedBy
